[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all decimals to like decimals by adding trailing zeros to have 3 decimal places.

245.360 + 12.475 + 98.240

= 257.835 + 98.240 = 356.075

**∴ The correct answer is 356.075.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given values: 245.36, 12.475, 98.24

Method: Vertical addition of decimals by aligning the decimal points.

⇒ 245.360

⇒ + 12.475

⇒ + 98.240

⇒ Total = 356.075

**∴ The correct answer is 356.075.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Like Decimals

Decimals having the same number of digits after the decimal point are called like decimals. For example, 0.500 and 0.125 are like decimals.

Alignment Rule

When adding or subtracting decimals, always align the decimal points vertically to ensure digits of the same place value are processed together.

Trailing Zeros

Adding zeros at the end of a decimal (after the last non-zero digit) does not change its value but helps in converting unlike decimals to like decimals.
